sources.boundary: The archive spans many years. Each run discovers only the archive index and fetches at most eight linked public messages; this is intentionally not a bulk email mirror.

sources.boundary: The full Discourse archive is large and mutable. A run ingests at most ten topics from the public latest-topic API, including their public posts.

sources.boundary: Only same-site research links exposed by the public landing page and two known public paper URLs are considered, capped at ten items.
sources.rights_policy: Public research material remains copyrighted by its authors unless the source states a license. The snapshot records attribution and does not assert redistribution rights.

sources.boundary: The public resource hub is sampled to at most ten same-site resources per run; external links and marketing pages are excluded.
sources.rights_policy: Public resources remain copyrighted by Fairgate or named authors unless an item states a license. No redistribution license is asserted.

sources.boundary: The official blog contains research and non-research material. The fetcher takes at most ten public blog posts and records that topical review is still required.
sources.rights_policy: Public articles remain copyrighted by Alpen Labs or named authors unless an item states a license. No redistribution license is asserted.

sources.boundary: The site and documentation set are broad. Three public papers are pinned and official blog discovery is capped so a run fetches at most ten items.
sources.rights_policy: Public papers and articles remain copyrighted by Babylon Labs or named authors unless an item states a license. No redistribution license is asserted.

sources.boundary: Only documentation, license material, and text source/script files are considered, capped at thirty files; Git history and binary artifacts are excluded.
sources.rights_policy: No repository LICENSE or COPYING file was detected at the pinned commit. No reuse or redistribution license is asserted; individual file notices, if any, continue to apply.
